title: Global solar PV O&M market reaches 348 GW as consolidation tightens and costs fall
gist: The global solar PV operations and maintenance market grew to 348 GW of assessed capacity by end-2025 (+61 GW year-on-year), with the top 15 vendors now controlling 57% of it, while North America shows falling contract costs in a maturing market and the Middle East/Africa shows near-doubling volume as an underpenetrated growth frontier.

insights.claim: The global solar PV operations and maintenance (O&M) market reached 348 GW of assessed capacity at the end of 2025, an increase of 61 GW year-on-year, based on tracking of more than 130 vendors across the Americas, Asia Pacific (excluding China), and Europe, Middle East and Africa.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Quantifies the scale and growth rate of the global solar asset-management services market, a directly investable market-sizing data point for O&M providers and infrastructure investors.
insights.locator: The global solar PV operations and maintenance (O&M) market reached 348 GW of assessed capacity

insights.claim: The top 15 global solar O&M vendors collectively added 41 GW in 2025, bringing their combined portfolio to 200 GW and raising their share of the total global O&M market to 57%.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Signals rapid consolidation among top-tier solar O&M providers, favoring scaled platforms and flagging smaller vendors as potential roll-up or M&A targets as the market concentrates.
insights.locator: Top 15 vendors tighten grip on a growing market

insights.claim: Full-wrap O&M contract costs in North America fell 18% year-on-year, reflecting a mature, competitive market where independent service providers (ISPs) are strengthening their dominant position.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Falling O&M costs pressure service-provider margins in North America even as volumes grow, indicating a maturing, price-competitive market relevant to O&M vendor profitability assumptions in the region.
insights.quote: In North America, a mature, competitive market is driving down costs while ISPs strengthen their dominance.
insights.locator: Full-wrap O&M contract costs fall 18% year-on-year in North America

insights.claim: Solar O&M volume in the Middle East and Africa nearly doubled in 2025, driven by a wave of new entrants chasing what Wood Mackenzie characterizes as an underpenetrated market opportunity.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Flags the Middle East and Africa as the fastest-growing regional solar O&M opportunity, attracting new entrants into an underpenetrated market worth watching for growth-stage investment.
insights.quote: In the Middle East and Africa, we are seeing a near-doubling of volume and a wave of new entrants chasing an underpenetrated opportunity.
insights.locator: Middle East and Africa O&M volume nearly doubles in 2025

insights.claim: Novasource Power Services retained its position as the world's largest solar PV O&M provider, ending 2025 with 38.4 GW under management.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Identifies the single largest incumbent in the sector, a scale benchmark for competitors and potential acquirers evaluating the solar O&M services market.
insights.locator: Novasource Power Services retained its position as the world's largest solar PV O&M provider

insights.claim: RES Energy Global Services, SOLV Energy, Solarig Energy Services and Recurrent Energy held their top-five global rankings alongside Novasource in 2025, with several pursuing active cross-regional expansion to defend their standings.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Identifies the stable core of top-five incumbents and highlights cross-regional expansion as their defensive strategy against rising challengers.
insights.locator: RES Energy Global Services, SOLV Energy, Solarig Energy Services and Recurrent Energy held their top five positions

insights.claim: BayWa r.e. Services and Origis Energy Services newly entered the global top-15 O&M vendor ranking in 2025, adding 2.6 GW and 1.8 GW respectively.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Identifies newer entrants breaking into the top tier of scaled O&M providers, potential emerging competitive or investment targets in the consolidating market.
insights.locator: BayWa r.e. Services and Origis Energy Services entered the top 15

insights.claim: Engie more than doubled its O&M fleet in 2025, leapfrogging six competitors to reach eighth place globally, driven primarily by a 172% expansion of its Americas portfolio.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Highlights Engie as the standout aggressive scaler in the Americas O&M market in 2025, a notable competitive mover for energy majors expanding their services arms.
insights.locator: Engie more than doubled its O&M fleet leapfrogging six competitors

insights.claim: Sterling & Wilson grew its O&M fleet 53% annually to reach 13.5 GW, climbing to sixth place globally on the strength of a dominant Asia Pacific (excluding China) position where it leads the region with 12.2 GW under management.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Identifies the regional Asia-Pacific-ex-China O&M leader and a fast-growing platform worth tracking for further regional expansion or as a consolidation target.
insights.locator: Sterling & Wilson recorded 53% annual growth to reach 13.5 GW

insights.claim: Among second-tier vendors, megaom (FRV's standalone O&M entity) posted the most dramatic growth rate in the report, expanding its portfolio by 243% to 3.8 GW globally and entering the top 30 for the first time.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Flags the fastest-growing sub-scale vendor tracked in the report, an early-stage platform that could become a future consolidation target or emerging competitor as the market keeps concentrating.
insights.locator: megaom - FRV's standalone O&M entity posted the most dramatic growth rate
